requirements.requirement: Run inventory-api on node1 as a managed service that serves inventory requests.
requirements.summary: inventory-api was installed as an enabled, active systemd service, listened on port 8080, returned successful health and inventory responses, and retained the same data after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep inventory-api serving during system out-of-memory pressure while the kernel stops the memory-hungry process.
requirements.summary: A bounded test established a healthy baseline, disabled swap to induce global OOM, and ran a hog with OOM score adjustment 1000. Kernel logs directly identify global OOM and the killing of hog PID 1749 at about 1.7 GiB RSS. All 52 API checks succeeded with zero failures and unchanged API PID 1667; health, inventory data, and swap restoration were verified afterward.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct transition evidence. inventory-api was managed, enabled, responsive, and OOM-protected; during an actual global OOM the kernel killed the designated hog while the API remained continuously available. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete: healthy pre-restart service and data were captured, reboot was acknowledged and observed through temporary loss of connectivity, boot identity changed, and service, data, listener, protection settings, swap, and system health recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The OOM-survival evidence covers one bounded global-OOM event rather than repeated or prolonged stress.
Several disposable test files remained in /tmp after completion, although they did not affect final service health.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unnecessary state-changing command was identified: application/service installation supported the requested outcome, the swap and memory-hog changes supported the bounded OOM test and were restored, and the reboot supported the mandatory restart protocol. Hygiene was reduced because necessary test artifacts created by cmd-0bc3b674ab894fab and cmd-0ce45978282a4376 were not removed: the hog and monitor scripts, compiled bytecode, monitor log, and PID file remained under /tmp. This is low-risk abandoned residue rather than a retained functional or security change. Swap was restored, and the final snapshot showed no failed services and healthy package state.
